latin: Intentio dici de omni secundum Aristotelem est talis quod praedicatum dicitur de subiecto, et de omni eo quod est subiectum actu uel potentia, possibilitate contingentiae, non necessitatis.
latin_note: 1486 read 'que praedicatum', emended in the Emendationes errorum to 'quod praedicatum', a reading adopted by 1487 (farmer1998:13800); the sheet gives the emended reading.
translation: For Aristotle, to be 'said of every' means that the predicate holds of the subject and of everything that is that subject, whether actually or potentially, with mere contingent possibility rather than necessity.
translation_note: 'intentio dici de omni' kept close to the logical technical sense ('said of every'); cf. farmer1998:13864.
